# Spotify in Rocola

All Spotify access goes through the `Rocola.Spotify` behaviour (`lib/rocola/spotify.ex`).
Adapters: `Fake` (dev/test default, no token) and `Web` (real API, stub). Never call an adapter directly.

## Recipe for a new Spotify capability
1. Add a `@callback` and a delegating function in `Rocola.Spotify`.
2. Implement it in `Fake` AND stub it in `Web` (`{:error, :not_implemented}`), same change.
3. Put queue/limit/vote rules in `Rocola.Jukebox`, never in the adapter.
4. LiveViews call `Rocola.Jukebox`/`Rocola.Spotify`, never `Req` or `Repo`.
5. Tests use the Fake (`Rocola.Spotify.Fake.reset/0` in `setup`), never the network.
6. `mix precommit` must pass.

## Real API rules the Fake must mirror
- The queue is add-only: no remove, no reorder. Skips, votes and per-guest limits live in Rocola's own
  SQLite queue; send Spotify one song ahead. Never add a "remove from queue" callback.
- Playback commands need Premium and an active device. Devices only appear while awake.
- Devices with `is_restricted: true` are shown unavailable and never get commands.
- Success is often `204 No Content` with no body: don't pattern-match on a body.
- `429` carries a `Retry-After` header (seconds): wait that long, then retry once.
- There is no push for track changes: poll `now_playing` (or broadcast over PubSub from the context that owns playback).

## Real adapter (later)
Authorization Code flow; access token refreshed only by `Rocola.Spotify.TokenServer`; never log or store
tokens elsewhere. Scopes: `user-read-playback-state`, `user-modify-playback-state`,
`user-read-currently-playing`. Endpoint details: `reference/endpoints.md`.

defmodule Rocola.Spotify do
  @moduledoc """
  The only way the rest of the app talks to Spotify. Callers use these functions;
  they delegate to the adapter set in `config :rocola, :spotify`
  (`Rocola.Spotify.Fake` by default, `Rocola.Spotify.Web` later).

  A new capability = a new callback here + `Fake` implementation + `Web` stub.
  """

  @type track :: %{
          uri: String.t(),
          name: String.t(),
          artist: String.t(),
          duration_ms: pos_integer()
        }
  @type device :: %{
          id: String.t(),
          name: String.t(),
          is_active: boolean(),
          is_restricted: boolean()
        }

  @callback search(query :: String.t()) :: {:ok, [track]} | {:error, term}
  @callback devices() :: {:ok, [device]} | {:error, term}
  @callback transfer_playback(device_id :: String.t()) :: :ok | {:error, term}
  # Add-only: Spotify's API can append to the queue but never remove or reorder.
  @callback add_to_queue(uri :: String.t()) :: :ok | {:error, term}
  @callback queue() :: {:ok, [track]} | {:error, term}
  @callback now_playing() :: {:ok, track | nil} | {:error, term}

  defp adapter, do: Application.fetch_env!(:rocola, :spotify)

  def search(q), do: adapter().search(q)
  def devices, do: adapter().devices()
  def transfer_playback(id), do: adapter().transfer_playback(id)
  def add_to_queue(uri), do: adapter().add_to_queue(uri)
  def queue, do: adapter().queue()
  def now_playing, do: adapter().now_playing()
end
defmodule RocolaWeb.Router do
  use RocolaWeb, :router

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {RocolaWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", RocolaWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", RocolaWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard in development
  if Application.compile_env(:rocola, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: RocolaWeb.Telemetry
    end
  end
end

defmodule Rocola.Spotify.Fake do @moduledoc """ In-memory Spotify for dev and test: ~50 seeded songs, 2 devices (one `is_restricted`), and simulated playback. Mirrors real API limits: add-only queue, restricted devices reject commands, playback needs an active device. No network, no token. """ use Agent @behaviour Rocola.Spotify @artists ~w(Aurora Lumen Nova Tidal Ember Vesper Quartz Harbor Willow Cobalt) @words ~w(Midnight Echo Golden Static Paper) @tracks (for {a, i} <- Enum.with_index(@artists), {w, j} <- Enum.with_index(@words) do %{ uri: "fake:track:#{i}-#{j}", name: "#{w} #{a}", artist: a, duration_ms: 150_000 + i * 7_000 + j * 3_000 } end) @devices [ %{ id: "fake-living-room", name: "Living Room (Fake Sonos)", is_active: false, is_restricted: false }, %{ id: "fake-locked", name: "Locked Speaker (restricted)", is_active: false, is_restricted: true } ] def start_link(_), do: Agent.start_link(fn -> %{devices: @devices, queue: [], now: nil} end, name: __MODULE__) @doc "Back to the seeded state (for tests)." def reset, do: Agent.update(__MODULE__, fn _ -> %{devices: @devices, queue: [], now: nil} end) @impl true def search(q) do q = String.downcase(q) {:ok, Enum.filter(@tracks, &String.contains?(String.downcase(&1.name <> " " <> &1.artist), q))} end @impl true def devices, do: {:ok, Agent.get(__MODULE__, & &1.devices)} @impl true def transfer_playback(id) do Agent.get_and_update(__MODULE__, fn s -> case Enum.find(s.devices, &(&1.id == id)) do nil -> {{:error, :device_not_found}, s} %{is_restricted: true} -> {{:error, :restricted_device}, s} _ -> {:ok, %{s | devices: Enum.map(s.devices, &%{&1 | is_active: &1.id == id})}} end end) end @impl true def add_to_queue(uri) do Agent.get_and_update(__MODULE__, fn s -> cond do not Enum.any?(s.devices, & &1.is_active) -> {{:error, :no_active_device}, s} track = Enum.find(@tracks, &(&1.uri == uri)) -> {:ok, advance(%{s | queue: s.queue ++ [track]})} true -> {{:error, :track_not_found}, s} end end) end @impl true def queue, do: {:ok, Agent.get(__MODULE__, & &1.queue)} @impl true def now_playing, do: {:ok, Agent.get(__MODULE__, & &1.now)} # ponytail: no timer; the first queued song starts playing immediately. Add a # Process.send_after tick that pops the queue when real-time playback sim is needed. defp advance(%{now: nil, queue: [t | rest]} = s), do: %{s | now: t, queue: rest} defp advance(s), do: s end 51: def live_view do 59: def live_component do 67: def html do 109: When used, dispatch to the appropriate controller/live_view/etc. defmodule RocolaWeb.PageController do use RocolaWeb, :controller def home(conn, _params) do render(conn, :home) end end defmodule RocolaWeb.PageControllerTest do use RocolaWeb.ConnCase test "GET /", %{conn: conn} do conn = get(conn, ~p"/") assert html_response(conn, 200) =~ "Peace of mind from prototype to production" end end defmodule Rocola.Application do # See https://elixir.hexdocs.pm/Application.html # for more information on OTP Applications @moduledoc false use Application @impl true def start(_type, _args) do children = [ RocolaWeb.Telemetry, Rocola.Repo, {Ecto.Migrator, repos: Application.fetch_env!(:rocola, :ecto_repos), skip: skip_migrations?()}, {DNSCluster, query: Application.get_env(:rocola, :dns_cluster_query) || :ignore}, {Phoenix.PubSub, name: Rocola.PubSub}, # Start a worker by calling: Rocola.Worker.start_link(arg) # {Rocola.Worker, arg}, # Start to serve requests, typically the last entry Rocola.Spotify.Fake, RocolaWeb.Endpoint ] # See https://elixir.hexdocs.pm/Supervisor.html # for other strategies and supported options opts = [strategy: :one_for_one, name: Rocola.Supervisor] Supervisor.start_link(children, opts) end # Tell Phoenix to update the endpoint configuration defmodule RocolaWeb.Layouts do @moduledoc """ This module holds layouts and related functionality used by your application. """ use RocolaWeb, :html # Embed all files in layouts/* within this module. # The default root.html.heex file contains the HTML # skeleton of your application, namely HTML headers # and other static content. embed_templates "layouts/*" @doc """ Renders your app layout. This function is typically invoked from every template, and it often contains your application menu, sidebar, or similar. ## Examples

defmodule RocolaWeb.Router do
  use RocolaWeb, :router

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {RocolaWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", RocolaWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", RocolaWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard in development
  if Application.compile_env(:rocola, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: RocolaWeb.Telemetry
    end
  end
end

Spotify has no push for track changes, so polling is the simplest option. If a playback-owning context is added later, PubSub would replace the polling.
- **Files:** `lib/rocola_web/live/request_live.ex`, plus the route change in `router.ex`.
- **Tests:** `test/rocola_web/live/request_live_test.exs` queues a track on the Fake and checks the banner changes. I rewrote `page_controller_test.exs` to check that `GET /` returns the page.
- **Left over:** the old `PageController` and `page_html` files are now unused. Then delete `page_controller_test.exs` too, since `request_live_test.exs` already covers the route.
